title: Record-Breaking Elemental Superconductivity in Tetralayer Kagome Borophene
authors: Yingnan Liu, Yan Liu, Renyu Duan, Menghui Wang, Meiling Xu, Hanyu Liu, Shoutao Zhang
abstract: Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature remains rare in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where strong covalent bonding often yields high phonon frequencies but insufficient electron-phonon coupling. Here, using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory, we predict tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) stabilized by ABAB covalent stacking, as a liquid-nitrogen-temperature elemental superconductor. With a predicted critical temperature of 102 K, TKB sets a record-high value among previously reported elemental superconductors. Unlike known high-Tc boron-based superconductors dominated by in-plane sigma-bonding states and high-frequency in-plane B-B stretching modes, TKB realizes an out-of-plane s-pz-bonding-mediated pairing mechanism, in which interlayer s-pz bonding states at the Fermi level are strongly coupled to low-frequency out-of-plane vibrations of boron atoms. These results reveal a distinct out-of-plane pairing channel in multilayer borophene and establish covalent stacking engineering as a potential route for high-Tc superconductivity in two-dimensional materials.
summary: This theoretical study predicts that tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) is a record-high-temperature elemental superconductor with $T_c=102$ K. The superconductivity arises from a unique out-of-plane pairing mechanism involving $s$-$p_z$ bonding states coupled to low-frequency boron vibrations. The work establishes covalent stacking engineering as a viable pathway for high-$T_c$ materials in 2D systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving high-temperature superconductivity in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where insufficient electron-phonon coupling (EPC) usually limits $T_c$.
main_result: The authors predict that tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) can be a record-high-$T_c$ elemental superconductor with a critical temperature of 102 K.
method: The study employs first-principles calculations combined with the fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory to model the superconducting pairing mechanism.
model_or_system: The physical system is Tetralayer Kagome Borophene (TKB) stabilized by ABAB covalent stacking. The theory focuses on the electron-phonon coupling mediated by out-of-plane $s$-$p_z$ bonding states interacting with low-frequency out-of-plane boron vibrations.
key_observables: Predicted critical temperature ($T_c \approx 102$ K), superconducting gap ($\Delta_{nk}$), and momentum-dependent EPC strength ($\lambda_{nk}$).
important_parameters: The optimal structure is TKB, which exhibits strong coupling ($\lambda = 1.78$) and is stabilized by the ABAB stacking.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on first-principles calculations and the Migdal-Eliashberg theory; the intrinsic properties are assumed, suggesting exfoliation is necessary for measurement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the TKB structure, orbital-resolved band structures, pCOHP analysis confirming OOP bonding, and phonon dispersion weighted by EPC strength, showing strong coupling at low frequencies.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the general problem in 2D elemental superconductors to proposing TKB, detailing the electronic structure and bonding mechanism, and finally calculating the record-high $T_c$ using advanced Eliashberg theory.
why_interesting: While focused on BCS-like pairing, the emphasis on strong coupling ($\lambda=1.78$) and the detailed orbital/momentum dependence of the pairing mechanism provides insights into how electronic structure dictates pairing symmetry, relevant for understanding correlated electron behavior.
